column3: Which best describes this graph: a large ring-like cycle / several disconnected pieces / a dense tangle?
column5: Two node groups in disjoint horizontal bands with no edges between them: a short chain of small nodes and a larger interconnected cluster containing small cycles; node sizes vary with no legend; uniform color within each group.
column6: Several disconnected pieces — the graph has exactly 2 connected components (20 nodes / 19 edges at the reference cell).
column9: The larger component's small internal cycles could suggest local loops; node-size variation is unexplained; in the NATIVE kk layout the two components are not clearly separated (component bbox IoU 0.036; 6.7% node interleaving) — the clean separation shown here is a property of the component-separated custom rendering; and the disconnected morphology itself is parameter-dependent: at cover (20, 0.50) the same data yields a connected graph with two 20-node cycles (E2).
column11: The 2-component structure is a computational fact of this parameter cell and is clearly displayed by the documented component-separated rendering; the same structure is much harder to read natively, and the morphology changes across the E2 grid. Graph structure, rendering, and parameter dependence are kept distinct here. Single-observer judgment.

column3: Which best describes this graph: a large ring-like cycle / several disconnected pieces / a dense tangle?
column5: One connected structure: a closed circuit of larger nodes with small-node tails; several short cycles; node sizes vary with no legend.
column6: Split judgment: the rendering reads as 'a large ring-like cycle', but the graph's cycles are noise-scale (longest basis cycle 6 nodes) and the underlying data has NO loop (H1 top persistence 0.140; r_1 = 1.45, below the stated convention of 3); with that computational context 'a dense tangle' is the defensible label — the graph rendering alone does not communicate it.
column9: The ring-like visual circuit is itself the misleading cue: Mapper graph cycles are not automatically topological loops in the data; nothing in the rendering distinguishes noise-scale cycles (6 nodes) from data-scale loops (16 nodes on the annulus); node sizes unexplained.
column11: The E2 no-loop sanity finding manifests directly in the artifact: an unprimed reading picks 'ring-like cycle' for a loop-free dataset. Cycle scale and the H1 diagram are what separate the readings, and neither cue is present in the graph rendering itself. The strongest representation-level ambiguity recorded in this inspection. Single-observer judgment.
